requirement_text.REQ-436:
The mounting precondition for REQ-437's unauthenticated mount, per decision 0028 s6 and REQ-434 / 0042. Split out of the endpoint entry so each is one agent turn. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate (INV-5, INV-8: a limiter that shares state with another mount, or grows without bound, is a defect on a multi-tenant platform). Where this text and the merged design (lib/letflow/design/req434-email-first-login-directory.md, s12) differ, the design governs; the amendments below are the design's s0.3 corrections D5, D6, D10, D11, D13 and D14 and REQ-VALIDATOR must accept them.
VERIFIED STARTING POINT: Letflow.Plugs.PublicReadRateLimit.Bucket (lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit/bucket.ex) exposes consume(key, capacity, refill_per_sec) over ONE named ETS table (:letflow_public_read_rate_limit) with bucket_key typed :global | {:ip, ip_address}, a check-then-write over :ets.lookup/:ets.insert (not :ets.update_counter/4), and NO eviction. Reusing it as-is would (a) share the :global bucket with /api/public, so flooding one mount would 429 the other, and (b) let an attacker grow the table without bound by submitting many distinct emails.
BUILDS: 1. A NEW sibling module, Letflow.Plugs.LoginDiscoveryRateLimit.Bucket (lib/letflow/plugs/login_discovery_rate_limit/bucket.ex), a GenServer owning its own named ETS table (:letflow_login_discovery_rate_limit); every key it writes begins with :login_discovery. The existing Bucket and PublicReadRateLimit are NOT modified (git diff empty, their tests pass unmodified). This is the 'mount-point-agnostic successor' reading of REQ-434 item 4, not a refactor of the existing Bucket (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D10). Shared with the existing limiter: the token-bucket algorithm (restated with a cross-reference comment), the Response.rate_limited + halt convention, 0028 s6 placement. 2. A plug Letflow.Plugs.LoginDiscoveryRateLimit (lib/letflow/plugs/), designed to run immediately after Letflow.Plugs.ClientIp (REQ-439) at the head of REQ-437's router chain, ahead of :match. The client address is conn.assigns.client_ip, falling back to conn.remote_ip when that assign is absent, and never a raw forwarded header (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D11: standing prohibition 8 is amended from 'keyed on conn.remote_ip' to the resolved client IP). The address is mapped to a bucket id with IPv6 aggregated to its /64 and an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address mapped to its IPv4 form (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D13). Order (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D13): the per-IP bucket is consumed FIRST; a refusal halts and does NOT touch the global bucket; only an IP-admitted request consumes the tighter global bucket. Both are checked before the body is read, so the 429 is input-independent for them. The per-email buckets are exposed as consume_email(email_key, kind :: :request | :send) for the endpoint to call after it computes the email key (the body is not parseable by a pre-:match plug without breaking the first-plug rule). Every refusal (IP, global, per-email) goes through ONE send_rate_limited/1 constructor, so the 429 status, headers (including a constant Retry-After) and body are identical by construction with no email-dependent content. 3. Bounded state (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D5, D13). Only LOSSLESS eviction: a periodic sweep deletes exactly the rows whose tokens have refilled to capacity (behaviourally identical to an absent row); a live (non-idle) key is never evicted, so a victim bucket cannot be refilled faster than its normal rate. Two key populations, two caps: email-kind keys (:email_hmac and :email_send) bounded by max_email_keys with a boot-time validate_config!/1 invariant (max_email_keys >= 2 * (global_capacity + ceil(global_refill_per_sec * (T_email_full_max + sweep_interval_s)))), and IP keys bounded by a hard max_ip_keys cap. At a cap, an inline sweep runs and, if still full, the NEW key is refused fail closed (an IP-key refusal does not consume a global token). consume is a compare-and-swap with bounded retries, failing closed on exhaustion, and inserts new keys with an insert-if-absent primitive. Capacities, refill rates, caps, sweep interval and retry-after come from application config (config :letflow, Letflow.Plugs.LoginDiscoveryRateLimit, ...) with the defaults of design s12.4, not hardcoded. 4. A fourth bucket kind, {:login_discovery, :email_send, h} (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D6): the per-address minimum send interval (default 1 token, refill 1/900 s, i.e. one notifier send per address per 15 minutes), consumed through consume_email(key, :send) by REQ-437's notifier task. Added to this entry rather than REQ-437 (design Q5). 5. Non-identifying outcome counters (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D14): one telemetry event [:letflow, :login_discovery, :outcome], measurement %{count: 1}, single metadata key outcome, emitted by this limiter with exactly :rate_limited_ip, :rate_limited_global or :rate_limited_email; metadata carries no email, key, IP, slug or tenant id. 6. It does NOT discharge the deferred authenticated Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit row in lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex (decision 0040) and does not modify AuthPipeline.

task.description: WF-02 step 01b hard gate: independently validate lib/letflow/design/req436-login-discovery-rate-limiter.md against every acceptance criterion (read the .md itself), no implementation code bodies, signatures/error shapes complete, consistency with merged req434 design s0.3/s12 (design governs), no planned edits to config/test.exs, config/runtime.exs, lib/letflow/identity*, login_directory*, routers/identity.ex (PR #2201), no new env var. Rule on design Q1 (headers), Q4 (extra config key inline_sweep_min_interval_ms) and the CAS/population-counting soundness (can the cap be exceeded or a live key evicted? any leak of reserved slots?).
acceptance_criteria: keys are namespaced and separate: a grep/test shows every ETS key this limiter writes begins with :login_discovery, lives in its own table, and that the existing Bucket's :global and {:ip, ip} keys used by /api/public are unchanged

independence test: flooding the login-discovery global bucket to exhaustion leaves a /api/public request unaffected (not 429), and flooding the /api/public global bucket leaves login-discovery requests unaffected; the same for per-IP buckets with one IP; both directions quoted

the (ip_capacity+1)th request from one client address (conn.assigns.client_ip; conn.remote_ip when the assign is absent) within the window returns 429; a spoofed X-Forwarded-For header does not change the bucket key; the global bucket trips independently of any SINGLE IP (driven from many distinct addresses) (design s0.3 D13)

ordering (design s0.3 D13): one IP sending 10x global_capacity requests is refused after its own ip_capacity and leaves the global bucket with at least global_capacity - ip_capacity tokens (global token count asserted directly); a second address is still admitted afterwards and never sees a :rate_limited_global outcome; an IP-refused request consumes no global token

IPv6 (design s0.3 D13): addresses sharing a /64 share one bucket, addresses in different /64s do not, and an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address maps to the same bucket as its IPv4 form (ip_bucket_id/1 table test)

the 429 response status, headers and body are identical for IP-bucket, global-bucket and per-email-bucket refusals and do not depend on the submitted email (byte comparison of the three); the plug refuses before the body is read (an invalid or unreadable body still gets 429)

bounded state, lossless eviction (design s0.3 D5): submitting 10x max_email_keys distinct per-email keys never makes the email-kind entry count exceed the cap (queried via :ets.info/size or a size function); a hot key keeps being limited after unrelated keys became idle and were swept, using an injectable now_ms clock (no sleeping); a non-idle key is never evicted; a swept key behaves as a fresh bucket

two caps (design s0.3 D13): distinct-/64 requests beyond max_ip_keys are refused without consuming a global token and without evicting existing keys, while existing sources are unaffected; validate_config!/1 accepts the defaults and raises for a configuration violating the max_email_keys invariant
consume never admits more than capacity under N concurrent callers (compare-and-swap property)

per-email bucket: the Nth request for one address across different source IPs trips the per-email request bucket, and a different address is unaffected; the :send kind (design s0.3 D6) has an independent bucket (one send per address then refused, request bucket unaffected)

outcome counters (design s0.3 D14): each refusal emits exactly one [:letflow, :login_discovery, :outcome] event with outcome :rate_limited_ip, :rate_limited_global or :rate_limited_email respectively and no other metadata key (no email, key or IP)

git diff on lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit/bucket.ex is empty; the existing PublicReadRateLimit tests pass unmodified
no email address, email key or IP appears in Logger output captured during the test file (INV-4)
`mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix test` for the touched areas and `mix letflow.check_boundaries` pass, real output quoted

result.summary: Independently read lib/letflow/design/req436-login-discovery-rate-limiter.md (664 lines) against all 14 acceptance criteria, the merged req434 design (s0.3, s5.5, s12, s15.2), response.ex, public_read.ex, infrastructure.ex and infrastructure_test.exs. Structure is strong: every criterion is traced, no implementation bodies, no TBD, no edits planned to config/test.exs, config/runtime.exs, identity*, login_directory*, routers/identity.ex, no new env var, infrastructure_test count 20->21 verified correct (20 ids listed today). CAS/population soundness verified: select_replace on the exact read tuple plus insert_new cannot admit more than capacity; reserve-then-insert (update_counter before insert_new, delete before decrement) keeps the count an upper bound on rows so the cap cannot be exceeded; the sweep guard is the same integer formula as consume and conditional per object so a live key is never evicted; every reservation is released on all paths except a process kill inside the two-call window (Q3, accepted, conservative). FAIL on one real contradiction with the governing 434 design (Q1 ruling) plus several spec/test-outline ambiguities that must be closed before build.

issues.description: Q1 RULING: REJECTED. 434 s5.5 requires Cache-Control: private, no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow on EVERY response from the route, success and refusal, and 434 s12.2 says send_rate_limited/1 sets 'the common security headers'. The limiter 429 is sent before the router (pre-:match) so the route's own header setter (as routers/public_read.ex set_response_headers/1, private there) never runs for it; with the design's default the limiter 429s would be cacheable by Cloudflare/nginx and miss Referrer-Policy/X-Robots-Tag. The design's reading (Retry-After only) overrides the governing design on the basis that no shared helper exists, but the header set is specified, not the helper. Fix: s6.6 sequence must put the three constant headers (cache-control 'private, no-store', referrer-policy 'no-referrer', x-robots-tag 'noindex, nofollow') plus constant retry-after in send_rate_limited/1, all cause-independent (byte-identity preserved); drop or rewrite s0 discrepancy note, s14 Q1; add the header set to T6 expectations (assert them on all three 429s); CORS stays with the upstream Cors plug.
s6 public surface: @spec config() :: %{...} is a placeholder, not a shape. Use the s2 type config() with the s6.1 key list (or a keyword/map with named keys and types).

s4 vs s7.1 spec mismatch: s7.1 declares sweep(now_ms, population \ :all) but the s4 @spec uses population() which has no :all (s2 type is :ip | :email). Define the type (population | :all) or drop the default and state sweep/1 as the all-populations arity.

validate_config!/1 inconsistency: @spec takes keyword() but s6.2 says 'keyword/map of overrides'; Bucket.init passes 'Application env'. State one input type (keyword) and how config/0 (a map) relates. Also s6.2 check 1 omits inline_sweep_min_interval_ms from the positive-integer list (the Q4 key must be validated), and does not require rate_u_s = round(refill*1_000_000) >= 1 (a refill below 5e-7 rounds to 0 micro-tokens/s and the bucket would never refill); add that check with its error message.

Q4 RULING: ACCEPTED as additive (434 observable behaviour unchanged; fail-closed cost bound is justified), conditional on it being added to validate_config!/1 (above) and listed in the s6.1 table as already done.

s7.4 / T7 hot-key scenario is self-contradictory: it says advance now_ms 'past the longest full-refill window' then sweep and expect the hot key to survive. With defaults a key drained to 0 refills fully in 300 s (request) / 900 s (send), so advancing past the longest window sweeps the hot key too. State concrete times: e.g. fill N keys with 1 token consumed at t0 (full after 60 s), drain hot key to 0 at t0 (full after 300 s), sweep at t0+120 s -> unrelated keys gone, hot key present and still 429; then sweep at t0+301 s -> hot key gone and a consume is :ok with full capacity.

s7.4 criterion 8 test (T8) asserts 'no existing IP row is deleted' while the cap-full path runs an inline sweep that deletes any idle row. The plan must require the earlier IP rows to be non-idle for the duration (tiny ip_refill_per_sec such as 0.0001 as s11.1 suggests for plug-level tests, stated explicitly for T8) so the test cannot flake on the real clock, and must also assert the inline sweep did not remove them.

s7.3: one shared {:login_discovery, :inline_sweep, :at} throttle row serves both populations, so an :ip inline sweep within 1 s suppresses an :email one. Either key the marker per population or state the shared throttle as intended (conservative: refuses rather than evicts).

s4.1/s7.1: sweep derives capacity/refill from config/0 per kind while consume takes caller-supplied capacity/refill. State that tests of sweep/eviction (T7, T9) must call Bucket.consume with the config values for that kind, otherwise a row can be swept against a different capacity than it was consumed under.

s5: add one sentence that the match-spec body must wrap tuple constants (double-brace) and that the literal key in the head makes the select_replace an O(1) keyed operation; otherwise an implementer can write a head that scans the table per consume.

Conflict recorded per core-directives: 434 s15.2 lists config/test.exs under Change; the design omits it per the PR #2201 restriction. Accepted (Q8) and consistent with the task, but 434 s15.2 stays stale until REQ-437/follow-up owns it.
